title: Global regularity or breakdown of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations

concept.text: A proof that smooth, globally defined solutions of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations exist in three dimensions for smooth initial data, or an example where they break down, as posed by the Clay Mathematics Institute. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
page.definition: For three-dimensional incompressible viscous flow, a proof establishes one of four alternatives on either all of space or a box that repeats in each direction. Global existence means that every admissible smooth initial velocity, with zero external force, gives smooth velocity and pressure for all time. Breakdown means that some admissible initial velocity and smooth force give no such global solution. The force may be zero. In all of space the solution must also have uniformly bounded kinetic energy. Incompressibility means zero velocity divergence. Smooth fields have derivatives of every order. At finite-time blow-up, speeds become unbounded as the time is approached.

goal.need: Aircraft designers and weather forecasters use equations that treat fluids as continuous. A simulation can follow a concentrating flow only down to its smallest resolved scale. Global smoothness would guarantee that viscosity keeps every admissible unforced flow smooth on the domain proved. A breakdown example would show how the model can lose smoothness in finite time, even from smooth data. Whether that flow occurs in nature is a separate physical question.

statements.context: Charles L. Fefferman’s official description of the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem gives two global existence alternatives and two breakdown alternatives.

completion.title: Clay recognizes a proof of any one of its four Navier–Stokes alternatives.
completion.criterion: CMI determines under §7 that a complete proof establishes A, B, C or D for ν>0 in three dimensions. A or B requires global C∞ velocity and pressure for every admissible smooth divergence-free initial velocity with f=0. C or D requires some such datum and admissible smooth force, possibly zero, for which no such global solution exists. On R³, all derivatives of the datum and force decay rapidly in space and in space-time, respectively, and the solution must have uniformly bounded kinetic energy. On R³/Z³, the datum, force and solution velocity are spatially 1-periodic, and all force derivatives decay rapidly in time.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Fefferman’s alternatives A–D and §§4–7 of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules.
completion.threshold_quote: we ask for a proof of one of the following four statements.
completion.basis: Clay requires qualifying publication, at least two years of examination and general acceptance before its own examination. OpenAI’s September 2026 forced breakdown theorems for R³ and the periodic domain have been checked in Lean. This confirms the formal mathematical result. Clay described the announcement as an apparent solution and has issued no ruling recognizing it. Alpöge and Buckmaster’s November 2026 unforced breakdown claim remains conditional on a numerical certificate. Their release omits both the certificate and its interval-arithmetic check, and the authors say the patched Lean package had not been rebuilt when released.

milestones.title: Every admissible smooth initial velocity has a smooth Navier–Stokes solution for some T > 0.
milestones.criterion: For ν>0 and zero external force, every admissible smooth divergence-free initial velocity gives a C∞ velocity and pressure on 0≤t<T for some T>0 depending on the datum. Use rapidly decreasing initial data and bounded kinetic energy on R³, or spatially 1-periodic initial data and velocity on R³/Z³.
milestones.set_by: The local existence theorem of Oseen and Leray in whole space and the periodic local existence theorem, both recognized in Clay’s official description.
milestones.threshold_quote: small time interval [0, T), with T depending on the initial data.

milestones.title: Every finite-energy divergence-free initial velocity has a global Leray–Hopf weak solution.
milestones.criterion: For ν>0 and f=0, every divergence-free u₀∈L² admits a global distributional solution u that is weakly continuous in L² and attains u₀ strongly in L² at t=0. For each finite T, u∈L∞(0,T;L²) and ∇u∈L²(0,T;L²). For every t≥0 it satisfies ½‖u(t)‖₂²+ν∫₀ᵗ‖∇u(s)‖₂²ds≤½‖u₀‖₂². On the torus the spatial norms are over one period cell.
milestones.set_by: Leray–Hopf existence theory; Definitions 1–2 and the existence theorems in Berselli and Spirito’s published treatment specify the weak-solution and energy conditions.
milestones.threshold_quote: There exists a Leray-Hopf weak solution u

milestones.title: Suitable weak Navier–Stokes solutions have zero one-dimensional parabolic singular-set measure.
milestones.criterion: For ν>0 and f=0, let u be a suitable weak solution, satisfying the local energy inequality. Let S consist of the interior space-time points where u is essentially unbounded in every neighborhood. Prove P₁(S)=0, where P₁ is one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure computed with cylinders of spatial radius r and time length r². This local test applies on R³ and on R³/Z³ and permits isolated singular points.
milestones.set_by: The Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg theorem, stated in Clay’s official description and recognized by the American Mathematical Society’s 2014 Steele Prize.
milestones.threshold_quote: Let E be the singular set of u. Then P1(E) = 0.

milestones.title: The mathematics community generally accepts a proof of one Clay Navier–Stokes alternative.
milestones.criterion: For the domain being tracked, a complete proof of its global-smoothness or breakdown alternative achieves general acceptance in the global mathematics community, as determined by CMI under §7(a)(i). OpenAI’s 2026 preprint claims breakdown on both domains with smooth forcing of compact time support and zero initial velocity; it is not peer reviewed. An unreviewed preprint submitted on 6 October 2026 reports mismatches between the prose and Lean proofs. The cited documents do not establish that this acceptance threshold has been met.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, §7(a)(i) of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules; this is the first evaluation stage before Clay’s detailed examination.
milestones.threshold_quote: First, a Proposed Solution must achieve general acceptance in the global mathematics community

milestones.title: A complete public proof establishes one of Clay’s four Navier–Stokes alternatives.
milestones.criterion: Give a complete proof of A or B for every admissible unforced datum on the chosen domain, or of C or D for one admissible datum and smooth force on that domain. Apply Fefferman’s conditions (4)–(7) on R³ or (8)–(11) for the periodic problem. A proof checked in a proof assistant confirms the theorem it establishes. If the proof derives breakdown only under a certificate hypothesis, establishing that hypothesis is part of the test.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, Fefferman’s alternatives A–D and the complete mathematical solution requirement in §5(a).
milestones.threshold_quote: we ask for a proof of one of the following four statements.

milestones.title: A Qualifying Outlet publishes a complete proof of one of Clay’s four alternatives.
milestones.criterion: A complete proposed solution of A, B, C or D appears in a Qualifying Outlet under §6. The ordinary route requires a refereed mathematics publication of worldwide repute with a named, contactable editorial board, an editor able to identify an appropriate referee, a published process for expert verification and inclusion in MathSciNet. The Board of Directors may approve relaxed conditions on the Scientific Advisory Board’s recommendation. The qualifying publication date starts the two-year period.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, §§4(a), 5(b) and 6 of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules.
milestones.threshold_quote: the Proposed Solution has been published by a Qualifying Outlet

milestones.title: Every sufficiently small admissible initial velocity gives a smooth unforced solution for all time.
milestones.criterion: For fixed ν>0 and f=0, prove global smooth existence for every admissible divergence-free datum in a ball of positive radius about zero in a stated initial-data norm. The radius is independent of the individual datum. The solution must have bounded kinetic energy on R³ or spatially periodic velocity on R³/Z³. The proof must specify the norm, its normalization and the smallness condition.
milestones.set_by: The small-data global existence theorem recognized in Fefferman’s official description, with whole-space estimates in Leray and a periodic Fourier norm criterion in di Dio.

milestones.title: A qualifying proof survives at least two years of examination and gains general acceptance.
milestones.criterion: At least two years have elapsed since the proof appeared in a Qualifying Outlet. It has survived rigorous examination by the global mathematics community for at least two years and achieved general acceptance in that community, as determined by CMI under §7(a)(i). The date of a preprint, announcement or Lean build cannot start the qualifying-publication period.
milestones.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute, §§4(b)–(c) and 7(a)(i) of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules.
milestones.threshold_quote: at least two years must have passed since publication, and (iii) the proposed solution must have received general acceptance in the global mathematics community

results.detail: The theorem applies to a class of initial data, so there is no sample size. Continuity in ℓᵖ at the initial time does not by itself establish smoothness there.
results.quote:
We obtain local existence and Gevrey regularity of 3-D periodic Navier–Stokes equations in
case the sequence of Fourier coefﬁcients of the initial data is in𝓁p (p <3 /2).

definition = "For three-dimensional incompressible viscous flow, a proof establishes one of four alternatives on either all of space or a box that repeats in each direction. Global existence means that every admissible smooth initial velocity, with zero external force, gives smooth velocity and pressure for all time. Breakdown means that some admissible initial velocity and smooth force give no such global solution. The force may be zero. In all of space the solution must also have uniformly bounded kinetic energy. Incompressibility means zero velocity divergence. Smooth fields have derivatives of every order. At finite-time blow-up, speeds become unbounded as the time is approached.". Reason: The definition excludes smooth external forcing from both breakdown alternatives and places unbounded velocity at the blow-up time instead of describing its approach.

goal.need = "Aircraft designers and weather forecasters use equations that treat fluids as continuous. A simulation can follow a concentrating flow only down to its smallest resolved scale. Global smoothness would guarantee that viscosity keeps every admissible unforced flow smooth on the domain proved. A breakdown example would show how the model can lose smoothness in finite time, even from smooth data. Whether that flow occurs in nature is a separate physical question.". Reason: The current rationale gives the prize amount and proof conditions but omits what regularity or breakdown would tell people who model fluids.

edit completion: title = "Clay recognizes a proof of any one of its four Navier\u2013Stokes alternatives."; criterion = "CMI determines under \u00a77 that a complete proof establishes A, B, C or D for \u03bd>0 in three dimensions. A or B requires global C\u221e velocity and pressure for every admissible smooth divergence-free initial velocity with f=0. C or D requires some such datum and admissible smooth force, possibly zero, for which no such global solution exists. On R\u00b3, all derivatives of the datum and force decay rapidly in space and in space-time, respectively, and the solution must have uniformly bounded kinetic energy. On R\u00b3/Z\u00b3, the datum, force and solution velocity are spatially 1-periodic, and all force derivatives decay rapidly in time."; set_by = "Clay Mathematics Institute, Fefferman\u2019s alternatives A\u2013D and \u00a7\u00a74\u20137 of the Millennium Prize Description and Rules."; set_by_kind = "prize"; threshold_quote = "we ask for a proof of one of the following four statements."; threshold_ref = 1; basis = "Clay requires qualifying publication, at least two years of examination and general acceptance before its own examination. OpenAI\u2019s September 2026 forced breakdown theorems for R\u00b3 and the periodic domain have been checked in Lean. This confirms the formal mathematical result. Clay described the announcement as an apparent solution and has issued no ruling recognizing it. Alp\u00f6ge and Buckmaster\u2019s November 2026 unforced breakdown claim remains conditional on a numerical certificate. Their release omits both the certificate and its interval-arithmetic check, and the authors say the patched Lean package had not been rebuilt when released."; refs = [1, 4, 5, 9, 21, 16]. Reason: The zero-force restriction excludes solutions expressly allowed by Clay, while the existing criterion mixes the mathematical statement with the status of one preprint.

edit m1: criterion = "For \u03bd>0 and zero external force, every admissible smooth divergence-free initial velocity gives a C\u221e velocity and pressure on 0\u2264t<T for some T>0 depending on the datum. Use rapidly decreasing initial data and bounded kinetic energy on R\u00b3, or spatially 1-periodic initial data and velocity on R\u00b3/Z\u00b3."; set_by = "The local existence theorem of Oseen and Leray in whole space and the periodic local existence theorem, both recognized in Clay\u2019s official description."; threshold_quote = "small time interval [0, T), with T depending on the initial data."; threshold_ref = 1; refs = [1, 6, 17, 18]. Reason: Oseen precedes Leray in the history of short-time existence, and the existing criterion mixes the theorem’s test with its proof history.

add milestone after m1: "Every sufficiently small admissible initial velocity gives a smooth unforced solution for all time.". Reason: Global smooth existence for sufficiently small initial data is a recognized result between short-time existence and global existence for arbitrary data.

This local test applies on R\u00b3 and on R\u00b3/Z\u00b3 and permits isolated singular points."; threshold_quote = "Let E be the singular set of u. Then P1(E) = 0."; threshold_ref = 1.
